utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Now it's Friday. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies and everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Foca was one of the biggest municipalities even in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I really have to remind both myself and you to make pauses, not to make the work of the interpreters more difficult. Is it correct that the population there, Serb and Muslim, was rather balanced numerically throughout the municipality, whereas in the town of Foca itself, the Serbs were more numerous, 50 per cent?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the census of 1991, there were about 21,500 Muslims, which is 52 per cent, Serbs accounted for about 19,500 which percentage-wise is about 45 per cent. 3 per cent were Montenegrins and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in town, there were 5,500 Muslims but 7,900 Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of those figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you were part of these party structures, as it were, to what extent did you know what was going on in the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which negotiations do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that negotiations on the fate of Yugoslavia and Bosnia and the fate of Bosnia in or out of Yugoslavia went on throughout 1991 and before the war in 1992, and then during the war as well, there was always a conference going on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Negotiations did take place before the war, too, and they ended on the eve of the war, or, rather, before the referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The referendum was held on 28 February and 1 March, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The final agreement on the transformation of Bosnia-Herzegovina into three constituent units, as a prerequisite for our acceptance of independence, was achieved on 18 March, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you put that question again and make it somewhat clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is how I'm going to deal with it. This was the chronology of these agreements. On 13 February, the first agreement was reached on the existence of three Bosnias. These negotiations ended on 13 March. Or the 18th of March, after the referendum. All three parties accepted everything that had been agreed upon except for what the armies would be like, whether it's going to be three National Guards or whether it's going to be a unified army. That is to say, that was the only question that remained unresolved. Everything else had been resolved?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We have the Lisbon agreement here. We are going to get to that easily. I'm just interested in knowing how much you knew.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that. I said that such agreements had not been reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of agreements at republican level, between myself and Mr. Izetbegovic, both on the division of power and everything else, weren't there negotiations underway at municipal level?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that what was also discussed was the establishment of two municipalities in Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb Democratic Party insisted explicitly at one point that the municipality should belong to the so-called SAO Krajina which had never been the case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Herzegovina, which had never been the case before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is a different matter altogether. Don't you agree that this entire area was called old Herzegovina, including my native region? Before the Berlin congress, all of that was old Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't Herceg Stjepan Kosaca have his capital in Foca? Are the remains of the old city not there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. It's in Stjepan Polje and that belongs to Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Line 15 on page 3 says that you said that it should be belong to the SAO Krajina, but you actually said SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We already corrected that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please correct that? You did not mean the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the SAO Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in practically all maps at these conferences, it had been envisaged that a larger part of Foca should belong to the Muslim constituent unit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday, I asked you whether you had distinguished between the commander of the Crisis Staff and the commander of the Territorial Defence, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. You did ask me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the commander of the Crisis Staff was Mr. Miro Stanic and the commander of the Territorial Defence, the Serb Territorial Defence, was somebody else?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time, there is no mention of the Territorial Defence in the documents, as it had existed before. There is only a reference to Miro Stanic and the other members of the Crisis Staff. We said that he had been appointed on 3 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could I find the documents I need? Let's show about two documents in order to see what it was like. 1D4237. Could we have that, please? Did you know Mr. Cedo Zelovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he head of the Territorial Defence for the Serb part of the municipality of Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, but take a look at this. See what this order is: Order to the unit of the military police. Up there it says: "Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Foca, the staff of the TO of the Serb Municipality of Foca." And this is what the order says, that together with the public security station, traffic be controlled, and vehicles without passes should not be allowed to move about, and also persons are not allowed to enter buildings. And can we scroll up a bit to see that the commander of the Territorial Defence is one person, that the commander of the Crisis Staff is another person?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please see the heading again so we see when this document was issued?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no date but you do know that Crisis Staffs existed until the end of May, and the Territorial Defence until 20 May because from the 20th of May onwards, it was the Army of Republika Srpska that came into being.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not accept this document in any way as a valid document. This is some kind of one-sided decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One-sided? You mean it only pertains to the Serb municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It's a decision of the Serb Democratic Party, to conceive of something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But yesterday you confirmed that to this day there is a Muslim municipality of Foca-Ustikolina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was set in the peace agreement, the Dayton agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, the Lisbon agreement had envisaged something far more favourable, then you get part of town and the Muslim villages. Had there not been combat you would have been given the greater part of the municipality of Foca, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really would not like to go into that part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please? You see, it's the same two men again, one is in the civilian authorities, the other one is the commander of the TO staff, and they are asking for lists of military conscripts to be compiled, to establish absolute control in their own territory and to prohibit any kind of abuse and unsoldierly behaviour, to submit lists of seized weapons and equipment to the staff of the Territorial Defence, on behalf of the Crisis Staff, it was signed by Miroslav Stanic and on behalf of the TO staff, Cedo Zelovic, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this document cannot be accepted as valid. It doesn't have a date. It doesn't have a number, and the content could have some kind of importance and meaning but only in a one-sided fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness. If the Crisis Staff was established on 3 April and abolished at the end of May, this could have happened only during those two months. Not before that, not after that, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is only an assumption. However, to accept this document as valid would be absurd since it doesn't have a date or a registry number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can these two documents be admitted under this number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you challenge the authenticity of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour, and of course the witness has pointed out a few things but they go more to the weight than anything else so we wouldn't have any objections, but of course it can only be marked for identification. And in this context, I just want to mention we have quite a number of these documents coming up, and it is really -- it's a burden to us not knowing what it is and only learn it here in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should put in a really vigilant effort not to present untranslated documents. There may come a time that the Chamber may prohibit you from using untranslated documents. Bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic. We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1684, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I really owe you gratitude but, please, do understand the fact that we are so burdened, we have so many documents, some we send at the very last moment for translation because we really have no choice. Could we now have 1D4238.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Colo, Izet, Redzo Pekac; are these people you knew, witness? They were represents of the Muslims from the village of Trosanj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, but the first and last names do ring a bell. It's not that I knew them personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the Council for National Defence of the municipality that is the Supreme Commander of Defence of the municipality made a -- reached a decision on 8 April that a state of emergency be imposed in Foca and that citizens are asked not to move about from 8 p.m. until 6 a.m. So there is a signature of Stanic on one side and the other signature is probably that of a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this document, and it could not be valid because there is no letterhead, there is no date, and there is no number under which it was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Obviously this is some kind of a press release. Could we have the next page? Can you see, Mr. Witness, that on 24 April, an agreement was reached between representatives of the Muslims of the village of Trosanj, and representatives of the civilian authorities of the Serbian Municipality of Foca and military authorities? Were you aware of this, namely that agreements on the surrender of weapons in illegal possession were reached with certain Muslim villages, with a view to ensuring the safety of citizens? Have a look at the document and let us know if you were aware of this. Can we scroll down? You don't have difficulties reading the Cyrillic script, do you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And item 5, all the Muslims from the village of Trosanj are guaranteed safety for their lives and property, and it is also stated that under 6, mixed commissions would be set up on the surrender of weapons which is to take place on 24 October -- of April, and that Muslims from other villages should not be allowed to enter the area and we have the signatures.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that on 24 April, the Serbian authorities from the Serbian part of Foca toured various villages to reach agreements such as this one?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it, and I have serious doubts about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this case, I agree that we could mark it for identification, but before taking a final stance on this particular document, I would like -- prefer to be able to read it first. The witness has not accepted anything in it, and, yeah, if it is authentic and if it is, when we can read it, fully related to the witness's evidence, then I would agree but I can't really at the moment see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's difficult to follow how this relates to the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we will not admit this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll look for another opportunity to have it admitted and by then we will have a translation. As for your question how it can be related to, well on 24 April the Serbs had that part of Foca under control and yet embarked on this exercise of reaching various agreements. And it is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You put that question to the witness. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did put it, but the witness was not aware of the existence of such agreements, which is also important for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am aware of it, or, rather, I am aware of the fact that such agreements did not exist. I'm aware of the fact that negotiations were not conducted with the various villages and the villages were not armed. It was a formulation of the events by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that a number of people were taken prisoner, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did mention a figure yesterday. It was between 600 and 650, in the correctional and penal facility. However, in addition to the KP Dom, there were at least 14 locations in the municipality of Foca which were designated either as camps or detention facilities. Let me mention but a few. If we first take Hotel Bukovica, there were civilians held there. If we go along the Drina downstream of the Drina, there was a Buk Bijela hydroelectric plant facility where civilians were also held. Admittedly most of them were women and children because the men had been taken to the KP Dom Foca. The next facility as we head toward the town is Brod facility, where civilians were also held. In the centre proper, we have the so-called Partizan conference hall where a number of women and children were held and where some of the most serious crimes were committed, women were raped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will be proving matters. You are merely saying things now, as you say that I am saying. Were you aware that on 1 March the Muslim armed formations took control of the town?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. You interrupted me. Let me finish off what I was saying earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that was not in answer to my question. My question had dealt with something else. You said what you wanted to say to the Prosecution, and I am here in charge of my examination. Do you agree that initially it was the Muslim forces that had taken control of the town?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, could you put a pause before you start answering? The interpreters have difficulty if you overlap. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D4239, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see here that on 8 April, an agreement was signed - we can't tell who it was on the Muslim side; on the Serb side it was Stanic - that the post office, pharmacy, the local radio station should be liberated forthwith, that all the units should be sent back home, that front lines should be abolished, that all the barricades should be removed, that joint observer groups and police forces should be set up on the principle of parity, that safety is to be guaranteed of all the -- all the vital institutions, that the safety of the KP Dom should be guaranteed and barricades removed? Who was it who erected barricades around the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not aware of the barricades being there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it who controlled the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, it was, I believe, the Muslim forces. That was the period of time when Donje Polje which is an area where KP Dom is located was defended by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the document further down. A working group is to be set up to deal with the line of separation and divisions. So you are being offered here a municipality of your own and, in fact, in all the maps being discussed at the time, most of Foca and the municipalities were supposed to belong to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is no veracity to this. This was a one-sided document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why don't you leave that to the Trial Chamber to decide upon. You were among the top echelons of the authorities there. Were you not aware of the fact that this was being discussed on 8 April at a time when Muslim forces controlled significant portions of the town?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under 12, movement of all and any units is forbidden. The TO storage facility should be restored to its earlier condition, fire is not to be opened as long as negotiations are ongoing, any armed groups are forbidden from going into neighbourhoods, inmates should be caught and sent back to the KP Dom. Were you aware of the fact that there were inmates, convicts, who had fled the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know, but in agreement with -- that was done in -- with the consent of the person in charge of the KP Dom and he was a Serb at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How can you know that? How are you able to know that warden of the KP Dom was in agreement with this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was Miro Stanic who said so to the Serb TV at Pale three years later, that the Serbs were among the first ones to be released. They were allowed to go back to their own municipalities and to join Crisis Staffs and Territorial Defence structures. He went on to say that next it was the turn of the Muslims and the Muslims from Sandzak to be released, the latter Muslims were perhaps able to reach their homes. As for the release of inmates, it did happen, and the population received this with apprehension. There was shooting accompanying one of these cases but it was more the case of a flight of prisoners rather than organised release.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we will have an opportunity to hear what Mr. Stanic said rather than hear your interpretation of his words. But why would they be chasing them down, the inmates who fled the KP Dom, if they were released as part of an organised exercise?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is a well-formulated document which is supposed to lend support to what the Serb Democratic Party and its staff is doing. This is to justify their conduct and actions but it is not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will not go into a debate about it. This is a document that wasn't published. It was a document between the Muslims and the Serbs. Can you see under 20 that it was agreed that joint mixed patrols of the army and the MUP were to be set up? This did not happen either, did it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is merely one of the provisions of this order or agreement which never took hold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, while you stated this is an agreement between the Muslims and Serbs, which was denied by the witness, and we have no basis to -- we have no idea about its foundation, whether it's just a draft or it's an agreement and who signed it. I don't think we have -- without having to have the assistance by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, we don't have -- we have no basis to admit it, in addition to the fact that this hasn't been translated. We will not admit this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do see a number at the bottom. I believe -- oh, no, I'm sorry, it's our number. Very well. We will look for another opportunity to have it admitted. Thank you. Can we have a look at 1D4235?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Witness, that you sabotaged or stone-walled the appointment of a Serb to the position of the commander of the TO. Mr. Sulejman Pilav, contrary to all the agreements reached, remained in the position of the TO commander through to the end?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never challenged it. I wasn't involved in the appointment of Sulejman Pilav to the position of the TO commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that according to the interparty agreement, this post was supposed to be taken up by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I can't remember what the allotment of posts was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that you don't recall that this was one of the main bones of contention between you and the Foca Serbs, the fact that you tricked them, they agreed to the appointment of all the Muslim cadres and you opposed this one post?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. According to the interparty agreement, based on the number of seats won, or number of votes won, and according to the agreement reached within the Municipal Assembly, i.e. the commission that was appointed, this is how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see, Mr. Witness, that on 3 October 1991, still Sulejman Pilav is the TO commander? Can we scroll down and we can see that the president of the Executive Board is asking for the umpteenth time that the appointment of one of the two Serb candidates go ahead? You were among the top echelons of the party in Foca, and you are telling us here that you were not aware of this dispute which was one of the most serious ones and sought to disenfranchise the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Truly, such a level of tensions in the relations is not something that I would remember, specifically in the month of October of 1991, as this document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the document? It says that it is seeking the removal of Sulejman Pilav and the appointment of one of the two candidates?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is acceptable. If the head of the police force was supposed to be a Muslim, then by all means the person at the helm of the Territorial Defence had to be a Serb. But I wasn't the one who was stone-walling this appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This can be marked for identification, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff? Do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D1685, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now can we look at 1D4234?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the agreement according to which posts were supposed to be distributed in Foca. Are you familiar with the name Fahrudin Suvalija; does it ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he one of the officials in the SDA city board in Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please help us and tell us whether it says here agenda, staffing issues, and the date is 27 June 1991, seven or eight months after the elections, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say here that under 1, Radojica Mladjenovic, on behalf of the Serbian side, and Halid Cengic informed the attendees of about the appointment of the chief of the security station and commander of the police and do we agree that the chief was a Muslim and that the commander was supposed to be a Serb, like in all the other municipalities, one was supposed to be from one people and the other from the other people, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that a good custom that prevailed even during the Communist reign?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really, not always. It depended on the municipality. Mr. Karadzic, I'm going to answer by saying this. I'm going to give you the facts. In the former Yugoslavia, in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Serbs always occupied a dominant position in the army, in the politics, among the executives of various companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's not go that way. I can easily prove to you that the Serbs were far below the 40 something per cent that was their share in the overall Yugoslav population but that's not Foca. Let's stick to Foca. That's something you should know. Do you see that there are also conclusions here as to what needed to be done, Muhamed Podrug and Zulfer Pjano are mentioned here as candidates for the prosecution, the Territorial Defence Staff, and so on and so forth. And can we now go to the following page, please? And now could you please show us the signature on that page? Do you see that on 27 June, Fahrudin Suvalija and Miro Stanic signed this document?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What document is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this refers to the points dealing with various positions, that the commander of Foca, the assistant commander for traffic and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a reference to the prosecution and the investigators with the Court. Zulfer and the other name, but you didn't read out a single Serb name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dragan Lausevic was the candidate for the post of public prosecutor, and it was agreed that on behalf of the SDA, the president of the Court was supposed to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, this document seems to be of two pages. Would you like to read it from the first page again? Why don't you show him the first page. The date seems to be 20 June and the date it was processed seems to be 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look starting with the agenda, and it says that Halid Cengic and Radojica Mladjenovic agreed what needed to be done and what persons should be appointed. Let's look at conclusion 2, please. You see that when it comes to the president of the Court, on behalf of the SDA, there were two candidates and one of them were supposed to be selected. Both were Muslims, Mohamed Podrug and Zulfer Pjano?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that that indeed was a proposal, but who were the Serb candidates?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The deputy public prosecutor was also Senija Sofradzija; that was the proposal, right? And as for the public prosecutor, was Dragan Lausevic, the president of the court was supposed to be a Serb and the public prosecutor was supposed to be a Muslim, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was then sent to the state bodies as an agreement reached between the two parties.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is a mere proposal. This is not the finalised state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it who became the president of the court in June 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb that was in that position previously was never replaced by anybody. He is still in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who is it who appoints judges?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Executive Board, the municipal Executive Board, who does that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is the People's Assembly who appoints judges, upon the minister's proposal, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we are talking about the municipal level, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, you asked what document this is about, when asked by the accused whether you saw the signatories. So now, are you in the position to answer the question what this -- as to the signatories? Let us show him the last part, second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There is no dispute about the signatories. I agree that those were Mr. Fahrudin Suvalija and Mr. Miro Stanic. I agree with that. But however we can see that this is the city board and we can see the SDS. I can't comprehend that Suvalija and Stanic could discuss such important positions in view of the fact that there was a municipality composed of Muslims and Serbs and that that municipality had all the bodies. There was a Muslim who was the head of the municipality and the head of the Executive Board was a Serb, Mr. Radojica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Witness, when it comes to the state bodies, were they not sent a list with two or more candidates pursuant to the interparty agreement? The municipality could not appoint judges, it was the Republican Assembly who did that on the proposal of the minister, and the minister in his turn had to receive proposals from the area. If somebody inappropriate was proposed as a candidate, the minister would not approve that, but in most cases, the interparty agreement was honoured, in most cases save for the case of the commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is just a proposal that was supposed to be sent to the republican bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking about the things that happened in Foca.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's then agree that this is just a proposal, that this formed -- that this is just a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1686, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D4231.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that the republican staff of Territorial Defence on 21 February 1992 wrote this letter to Foca municipality, to the president of the Executive Board, and it says here the Municipal Assembly of Foca is providing an opinion on the appointment of the commander of the Territorial Defence of Foca, and it says that Sulejman Pilav was in a the position from 1989 without my approval and agreement. In -- according to our criteria, he does not meet the requirements for that post. What was his profession?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was a nurse and he was also a law student.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Pilav was older than us, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a year or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it was rather late for him to be a law student in 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he could still be a student, a part-time student.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please? You see here, in the second paragraph, where it says it is inadmissible in a state with the rule of law that Captain First Class Sulejman Pilav is performing the duties of the TO commander in Foca without any official appointment and without any adequate education. [As read] "Please urgently send me a proposal for the appointment of a new TO commander. Here enclosed, please, find copies of facsimiles and interparty agreement which shows that what you're requesting from me is a strict adherence to the legal procedures and that you, yourself, are in breach of such practices." And the signatory here is Mr. Vukosavljevic. Did you know that the person held a position which was supposed to be given to Serbs and which was supposed to be occupied by a person with adequate education, that this is contrary to all agreements in 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not aware of this letter but I do know that a majority in the SDA party agreed that there should be changes there, and it was never our view that there was something to contest on our part, and I've already told you that if a Muslim was the chief of the public security station, it was only logical that the chief of the Territorial Defence was a Serb. For example, Mr. Cedo, who was a moderate person and we would have all accepted him. I apologise, let me finish. I don't see that this was a major sticking point that would necessarily have led to conflicts and rifts among the peoples.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, do you agree, witness, that the political life does not tolerate such tricks and deceits? If something is agreed it should be implemented?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. However, in political sense, nothing is ever, ever ideal. I'm not contesting that this should have been done in a more effective way, in a faster and more efficient way. That this would have avoided unnecessary problems among the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In addition to the fact that this hasn't been translated, speaking for myself, I doubt whether -- I'm not sure if this document is relevant and whether it relates to any part of the witness's evidence in one way or another. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we will not admit this. After all, it boils down to the efficient conduct of your cross-examination. It turned out that you wasted time. Come to your real issues, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency, but my idea is to show why a conflict happened there, whether the seed of that discord was planted there, in their midst, or was it imposed from above, from the republic, and this has a direct link with the charges brought against me. I didn't even know anything about all those happenings over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in mind, Mr. Karadzic, the invaluable advice from Judge Robinson yesterday -- I'm sorry, Judge Morrison. It's Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, tell me, I don't know whether I asked you this yesterday: Do you know that Mr. Halid Cengic who is mentioned in here, in 1990, during the Communist reign before the elections in Ustikolina, in the mosque, set up the first unit of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that you didn't know that or that he did not set it up?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. He didn't set it up and I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that he didn't set it up if you didn't know it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure I would have learnt about that. My village is not far from Ustikolina. I used to pass that way quite often, and I spent some time working in Ustikolina and, really, that did not take place. It would have echoed, it would have been heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If it did happen, it had a lot of impact among the Serbs, did it not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what you're giving me is a false thesis and you're trying to trap me into that. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you say that in early April 1992, I visited Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never said that, I never said that you visited Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say some Serbian politicians from the republican level including Karadzic visited Foca at the time. You said that in -- on 27 November 2000. And the case is IT 97-2-2, on page 186.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember that I ever said that. First of all --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Witness, the interpreters couldn't hear your last part. Could you repeat your answer kindly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't remember that statement, that I said that. I never saw you in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Perhaps the document could be put to the witness so that he can see what he, in fact, said, where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a 1D number but if you can bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the date is 27 November, then it should be his sixth 92 ter transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3335, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1186. I don't know the number in e-court but in transcript it is 1186. Page 7 in e-court. I'm going to read it out and then it can be interpreted. [In English] [As read] "Q. Did politicians from the republic level appeared in Foca in that time period? "A. Yes, especially those who were born in Foca. Among them were Mr. Velibor Ostojic and Mr. Maksimovic and they were often visiting Foca. Occasionally Mrs. Plavsic would visit as well. I think she was, out of the three leading figures, Karadzic, and the third one who died, I can't remember exactly -- Koljevic -- so she was the one who visited most often." [Interpretation] You mention me here as a colleague of Professor Plavsic's, not as a man who visited Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was interpreted to me now is the truth. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that in the beginning of April, Mrs. Plavsic came to Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was this holiday, it was before April. I think it was January or February. It was -- it was Trinity Day, one of your holidays, and this gathering was held at the Sutjeska stadium where you held your first gathering and where you introduced the Serb Democratic Party of Foca in September 1992. That is when Mrs. Plavsic was in Foca, on this holiday of yours. Trinity Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I remind you, Mr. Witness, of course you don't have to know about this, that in all Christian churches, Trinity Day is 50 days after Easter, and that can certainly not be later than mid-July.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise if I confused the names but there was this holiday of the Serbs that brought the Serbs together in this early period of 1992. Mr. Karadzic, I do remember that very vividly because my apartment is not far away from the Sutjeska stadium, when I heard shouts, gunshots, I really felt very worried and I was wondering what was going on and what was in the making. The iconography was varied. There were people from Serbia there. The Chetnik movement of Ravna Gora was being mentioned. Also there were shouts that Serbs would tell the Muslims who they were, that they would defend their own country, their own land, the Serb Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the summer of 1991, that could not have happened. Especially when the Pentecost is being observed, there can be no shooting whatsoever. Are you talking about a political meeting or gathering or are you talking about Pentecost?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are going to see what it was when we hear Mr. Stanic's transcript and then I'm going to apologise if I misstated this Serb holiday. I don't know when it actually does happen. I know for sure that the 7th of January is Christmas Day. I'm not sure of any other dates, as far as Serb holidays are concerned. However, this event had to do with some holiday, some Serb holiday, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you saw an M-48 rifle in the hands of Mladen Zecevic, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that M-48 rifles have been decommissioned in the JNA, actually 15 or 20 years ago, they had been decommissioned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a hunting carbine resembles an M-48 to a great extent?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was never interested in weapons. However, I only knew M-48 rifles because that is what I had been issued with as I did my military service. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could the Chamber move into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 4226, page 2, and 227, in that I'd like page 3. Do you remember giving these statements? Is it correct here that Muhamed Kameric, nicknamed Meca, entered the health centre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A Muslim wearing camouflage uniform and armed with two hand grenades; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he had nothing to do with this. I happened to be there and the director, Sadinlja and two drivers and a colleague, Biljana Popovic and Vojkan Slavica, who were two nurses, we were highly surprised. We were wondering how come he showed up there and we were wondering what he wanted. I am sorry. As for this statement, we haven't done anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, witness, do you see this detail that you referred to when speaking to the Bosnian authorities? You did not tell the investigator from The Hague about that, this detail is not contained in your other statement, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am trying to say that I stand by all the statements I gave to the organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that I gave to the investigators of the Tribunal in Sarajevo, and, of course, here before the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, the fact remains that what you said to the Bosnian authorities, namely that Kameric, Muhamed, wearing a camouflage uniform entered the health centre in camouflage uniform and with two hand grenades. That is something that you did not repeat to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably didn't ask me about that. I really cannot recall that detail now. I have to tell you that it's been a long, long time, if we look at the period that we are talking about now. You have to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What kind of uniform was Muhamed Kameric wearing?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned. I think it was a dirty camouflage uniform. However, as soon as he came in, I was taken out of the basement for these interviews and that's how I saw him. Otherwise I wouldn't have seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that this Zecevic came wearing a JNA uniform, and you say that someone, either he or someone else, called out your name from the basement, that you should go to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, Zecevic was not calling out my name. He was an elderly man. (redaction)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, this group was commanded by Cicmil. I think that he was --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are we in open session? Because we are discussing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's noted. Could the Chamber move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, is it true that you stated that the person interrogating you did not physically mistreat you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We knew each other from before. We would go frequently on missions in the field. He on behalf of the police force, and I on behalf of my profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Goran Kukavica was also among those arrested. Was he a Serb?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was our driver, and he was in a mixed marriage.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: He was born to a mixed marriage, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I don't think I've properly understood your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, there were three or four Muslims there who were told that they were free to go home, whereas others were arrested. So --

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we go back to private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, Your Honour, it's safer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time. We will take a break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more question, please, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, if the Serbs attacked Foca, why would they ask the Muslims about their whereabouts during the attack?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first question put was one inquiring about the whereabouts of the Muslims on the eve of the attack of Foca. Why would this question have been put to them if the Serbs had attacked Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was the tactics that they employed in their interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. After the break we will show the lists of those who were released after having gone through the first interrogations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will take a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this is my thesis: Interviews were conducted in detention. Certain individuals were released home after having been interrogated. Others were released even if they were not interrogated, if somebody guaranteed for them. And others were not released but were transferred to Kula or elsewhere and were released at a later date. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your thesis and it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look up 65 ter 14733?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in mind pause, sir, before you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to cast a glance at this list? It is a list of prisoners of war of Muslim ethnicity to be released from the KP Dom in Foca in order to be exchanged for captured Serbs from Konjic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a moment. Let us see the heading, the number and the date when it was written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date, the signature and the stamp are at the bottom. Colonel Kovac. The prisoners were taken over by Lieutenant Milos Andic, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, yes. But this isn't accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, you said this is not accurate. Could you expand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down or rather up? I'd like to go from number 1, if I can. Let me start from number 4. I am familiar with the name. This individual worked with me. The particulars are accurate. He was exchanged in the late autumn of 1992 for captured Serb civilians at Trnovo front line where fighting was going on. That's true. Under 6, Salih Music, the same applies to him. Under 13, it should be 13, Abid Sahovic, son of Avdo born in 1936, the same applies to him, the particulars are correct. I know the three of them were to be exchanged for Serbs but not in Konjic, rather at the Trnovo front line. That's true. The remainder of them stayed in the camp for a long period of time. Some of them were exchanged, namely Suljo Haznadar, under 12. He stayed on until, I believe, 6 October 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we show the first two lines, top, upper part of this document? Could you kindly read the two lines, for our benefit? Because the accused hasn't offered us the translation of this document in order for us to understand. If you could read those two lines so that the interpreters can interpret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [As read] "List of prisoners of war of Muslim ethnicity who are being released from the KPD Foca to be exchanged for Serbs prisoners from Konjic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could read also the last two lines? Shall we show him the last lines? Further down, further down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. [As read] "The prisoners of war were taken over by members of the command of the 2nd Light Infantry Brigade, Konjic, under the command of Lieutenant Milos Andric. 8 December 1992." When it comes to the 8th of 12 -- of December, I would like to -- this is something that reminds me of a completely different set of individuals who were released under the pretext of having to be released -- to be exchanged in Konjic. But, in fact, quite a different fate befell them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1687, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here is another example, 65 ter 14739.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have a look. The date is 18 July 1992. It reads that Alic Mirsad should be released after being checked because he did not participate in the hostile activity in Foca. So you can see here that the individual's background was checked, and it was decided that he should be released and set free in Foca.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I myself don't know Mirsad Alic and I could not state for a fact that he was in the KP Dom in Foca to begin with. I don't consider this to be a reliable document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why, Mr. Witness? Why is that? This document was produced in July of 1992. Why do you not consider it reliable?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because a day earlier, something different happened at the KP Dom, something dangerous, if I may put it so. A large group of 45 Muslims were taken out and disappeared without a trace. Later on, in a grave, a great many of them were found. They were killed from firearms at point blank with a shot to the head. That happened a day earlier. On 17 July. No, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, it was on 17 September. I apologise to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we will come back to that if we have time enough. Please do not go into details. Are you challenging this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that he was in the camp or that he was released. I do challenge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do concede that individuals would be released?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would be taken back to their cells after having been interrogated. They would be tortured and they would then be taken out and disappear without a trace. Probably killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of anyone who was forever -- for whatever reason released and stayed in Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have confirmed that Enes Zekovic was released but he did not stay in Foca. He went to Germany with his wife, and I think that he was released because he was blackmailed for his property. It happened also with Lojo Dzevad, the mine manager, and a couple of others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, why don't you furnish the Prosecution with evidence to that effect and answer my question? Can this be admitted? Mr. Witness, you are exaggerating, you are not honest and you are not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have been called here to tell the truth and nothing more than the truth, truly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karadzic should not make this kind of comments but in relation to this document, unless I'm missing something, there is no reference to a detention of this gentleman in the KP Dom. At least I cannot see any. So -- but I do not object against the admission of this document because it looks authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1688, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let us now see an example when a person was released without having been interrogated. Can we now look at 65 ter 14742. 14742.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P3346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that there is a translation which will make things easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look, witness, on 9 May, there is still a Crisis Staff in place. There is no Serbian army there. You see that this is a list, and since there is a translation I don't need to read. However, it says: [As read] "Pursuant to the Miljevina Territorial Defence and the approval of the 7th Battalion commander, following persons shall be released without interrogation." And they are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, yesterday we discussed this document. Do we have to go over the same document again today? I've told you, I dwelt upon the name under 13. I explained what his lot was, how he disappeared, how he was buried ultimately, and as for the rest of them, my conclusion was that all these people from the list were killed. They never turned up alive. I never claimed that they were all in KP Dom, that they had all been brought there. This is a list containing the names of the persons who were by and large poor. They were miners in the coal mine in Miljevina. They were not interested in politics, in party affiliation, they were in their own homes. They were, most of them at least, elderly, frail. I knew most of them very well because I lived with my family in Miljevina for 15 years and I know the area very well. But I would like to point out that younger people from the list were in the camp, like, for example, I would say that Senad Dzanko is a wrong name. There was Edin and Elvedin Dzanko, there were two brothers, younger men and together with another person, Adil, who was a bachelor in economics in August 1992, they were brought out from the camp and they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have proof of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Adil's body has been exhumed already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he could not have been killed any other way? The only way he could die was by having been taken out of the camp and killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm claiming. In the middle of the day, guards stormed his room and the room of -- where the Dzanko brothers were. They took them to the metal or to the iron gate, through which we either entered or exited from the perimeter of the KP Dom, I described them as resounding in a very typical way that made an impression on all of us. And they were standing there for a long time. And my room or my cell, number 12, its windows overlooked the gate directly, and they were standing there for a long time, the police came, they took them out, and from then on, every trace of them was lost. After a long time, I had an occasion to be in Sarajevo after I was released from the camp to meet with the parents of all of them. Dzankos' mother was as white as a sheep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that people, after having been released, joined the BiH army and was that your case as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. According to the rulings of the International Red Cross, and according to some other conventions, we were not duty-bound or forced to become member of the BiH army. I personally never joined the BiH army after having been released from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the others? Did the others join the army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know a single person who joined the army. I apologise. They were all thin, exhausted, we were all on the brink of survival. I spent six months and three days in the camps and it took me six months to recover. How could I have become a member of any military formation? And the same applies to all the others. You are not even asking me about the conditions that we suffered in the camp. You've never asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, those who were released on 9 May, are you saying that they were exhausted to such an extent that they could not recover sufficiently within the next two or three months to join the BiH army and to be killed in fighting, are you claiming that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially in view of the fact that all these men were elderly, frail, and infirm. I am telling you that I lived in Miljevina for 15 and more years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's enough, we don't need to go into all those details. I would like to call up 65 ter 15795 now. Were these people in the camp in Foca and were they exchanged on 30th of October 1992, or were they killed? And it says here that they were exchanged? At the bottom you can see that Milenko Vukovic, commander of the Konjic military police took the detainees over and it was approved by Colonel Kovac.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that this exchange never took place or do you agree that it did? The decision was taken on 29th and on the 30th, the exchange took place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this didn't take place in Konjic but in the Trnovo front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1689, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, what did you say about the time when the Serbian Municipality of Foca started functioning? When was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document that we saw, that was on 31 December 1991. That's when it was established and it has been functioning ever since.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Defence puts it to you that it was then that it was proclaimed and that it did not become operational before the war started. And now let's look at 1D4211. 1D4211.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Hasn't been released, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not notified either.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be in e-court. I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, witness, that on 7 April, the president of the Serb Municipality of Foca, Josif Milicic says under item 1 on 7 April 1992, all bodies of the Serbian Municipality of Foca started working and then an appeal is launched to the Serbian people and all citizens to preserve peace, not to buy into provocation, not to move out of Foca, and under 3 it says that units of the Territorial Defence, together with the members of the public security station, will prevent the presence of paramilitary formations, that they will inform citizens that it is not against the holding of rallies but that they should be reported in order for the citizens to be protected. Do you know if there were any paramilitary formations that Mr. Milicic refers to and says that they would forbid their presence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with Mr. Milicic's name but I'm not aware of this document. I never saw it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Serbian Municipality of Foca appealed to the citizens, both Muslims and Serbs, not to move out of Foca, and there is another document that has been admitted, it actually appealed to them to return to Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be accepted but I would request a different explanation. When they were called to return, that was another trap. They wanted just to increase the number of those who were caught. There was an invitation of that kind heard in Foca and elsewhere. They were called to return because they would be safe. Some people believed that, but they fared badly. There was another provocation entitled, "A journey to an uncertain freedom."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that out of the 20.000 -- 28.000 and something Muslims, not more than 5- or 6- or 650 were arrested, many of whom were released immediately after checking or they were exchanged but you are claiming here that the plan was for -- to arrest all of them. You are under oath, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness did not say that. He actually started when this question was put to him for the first time this morning he started to give a lot of more details where people were detained in other places and he was then stopped by the accused. He did never say that out of this 28.000, only 500 to 600 or 650 were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you say yesterday and repeated it today that up to 650? How many Muslims were taken prisoner in the April conflicts?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat what I've already said. Between 600 and 650 were in KPD. However, in addition to the KPD, there were other numerous places in the municipality of Foca, both camps and other places of detention, where smaller or larger groups were kept. I was just going to mention motel Bukovica and Partizan where women were raped but you interrupted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you saying that the fact that civilians were placed in the barracks in Filipovici and in the school, for their protection, that these people were also detained?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although they went there of their own will to seek shelter, you're saying that they were detained?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of a shelter is a school? Everybody knows only too well what a school is for. They were taken there from their own homes, from their houses, from the streets. They been captured and arrested and let me say something about the Filipovic barracks. There were no barracks there. There were military depots there on the hill slope some fuel was kept there and those facilities which were military facilities, had been built several years before the war by a civilian company, and the employees of that company were guards guarding the facilities. When the war broke out and when the Muslims from Foca started fleeing towards Ustikolina and Gorazde, they found themselves very close to those facilities that you refer to as Filipovic barracks. Filipovici did not have any barracks so that would be that. That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But were they detainees or did they seek shelter there of their own will?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abid Sahovic whom we saw on the list of those who were exchanged was one of those detained. Please, let me finish my thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed. Please carry on. Do you have more to say, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just wanted to elaborate, and to tell you that a Mr. Abid Sahovic was on the list that we saw just a little while ago. He was in his house when he was taken prisoner and brought to that shelter that Mr. Karadzic refers to which is only half a kilometre away from his home. Then he was taken to the Foca camp and then he was exchanged at the Trnovo front line. He was a very frail person and during his stay in the camp he sought medical assistance and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, we have another witness who claims that they were not detainees. Are you aware of the second document or declaration which was an appeal for the people to return? And you're saying that in all the municipalities where it was heard that it was a trap?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a clever deceit on behalf of the Serbian Democratic Party and the political leadership. Unfortunately it was perilous for many Muslims who returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Muslims and Serbs were prevented from leaving Foca or Srbinje as it was also known at first, but then they were issued passes to be able to travel?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you speaking about Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Serbs as well.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the Serbs. As for the Muslims, some of them would receive a pass or permit of the sort but only rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 16753?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous one can be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1690.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I meant 1D4211. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have a look, Mr. Witness. This is a pass issued to Armin Pilav allowing him to travel to Belgrade and Skopje. Can we have the next page, please? The date is 26 June, 1992. This is to the name of Lejla Pilav; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page? Same here, in the early days, they wouldn't issue passes to anyone and at a later date they would issue passes allowing movement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to say what I have to say about what we saw. This is a family Pilav, Hasan, husband, then the lady doctor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then their children, Armin and Lejla. They were held in the Livade camp from where they were transferred to the KP Dom Foca. Dr. Pilav's husband, Hasan, was ill. He had had a heart attack. She wrote numerous letters requesting of all those who had superior positions in KP Dom Foca, that they be released from there. After a number of discussions within the compound of the Foca Dom, they were released, though there were requests for her son Armin and husband Hasan to stay behind. She was insistent, however, and somehow an agreement was reached. Now that they received, at a later day, passes from, as it says here, the Foca public security station, this is something that I'm seeing for the first time now but do I not rule it out as a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1691, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see what was the basis for issuing them with the pass? Can we look at P2642 briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know that on 22 May, an agreement was signed in Geneva placing the parties under an obligation to allow civilians to cross from one side to the other and travel freely?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the date you mentioned in relation to Geneva?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 22 May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of such an agreement. Even if it had been signed, it would not have been complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. In Foca, not complied with in Foca or anywhere in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anywhere in Bosnia, wherever there was a presence of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how would you be able to know that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do know from the period after my release, and I do put the various pieces of the mosaic together of what happened in Bosanska Krupa, Bosanski Petrovac, Bosanski Novi, Brcko, Bijeljina, Banja Luka, Foca, Cajnice, Visegrad, Zvornik, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, were you in all these locations?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But we have figures, these are municipalities that you ethnically cleansed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's stick with Foca. You were there. Let's see what we have here on the 18th of June, eight days before the family Pilav was released. Do you see that it says here that the civilian and military authorities had to that date banned both Muslims and Serbs from leaving Foca municipality? It is stated that families have the right to stay together and that both the military and civilian authorities should allow all citizens who had not had a run-in with the law to travel, et cetera? Do you see item 2 where it says that citizens of Muslim ethnicity stated that they were betrayed and abandoned by their leadership and that this was an additional incentive for them to leave Foca municipality? Can we have the next page? Do you not see that it was on the basis of this request by Mr. Stanic, president of the War Presidency, so at this stage we no longer have Crisis Staffs, we have the War Presidency, that people were allowed to travel and were called to return?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure this was not the way things worked. Nobody was allowed to leave Foca unless the person was first interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
