utterances.text: However, there were even bigger restrictions for Serbia when it came to entering Croatia, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: You should know that better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say that in March 1992, the Serb forces set up a few check-points around the village. First of all, let me ask you who was it who prepared you in Bosnia for these testimonies?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: I wasn't prepared by anybody. I'm just here to tell you what I know and to repeat what I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you choose the wording, the collocations, the words? Did you choose those words, or were they suggested to you by somebody from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: I'm not with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what Serbian forces existed in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: I don't understand when you say Serb forces. What I meant was that, that people already wore uniforms in the then Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they were all troops of Serb ethnicity, and since we in Biljani were in the centre of the village, around us in 1992 in March, they set up some four or five check-points and they set up guards around the village to have us under control, to have us right before their eyes all the time. From April on, I did not set foot out of my village. If I did go anywhere, it was not further than one kilometre from the village which means that my movements were restricted. I could not go anywhere. I just couldn't leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that the JNA, composed primarily of Serb soldiers, set up some check-points in your municipality? Am I interpreting your words properly?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: Yes. It is true. At the exit from Biljani to -- towards Sanica, on the bridge across the Sanica, they set up a check-point. Another one at Velagici towards Kljuc, those were the main roads and there were two or three other check-points or guard posts around Biljani. As I've already told you already the month of March they were in Gologlav and Lunjevo. Those check-points were already set up there. That was already in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to that. Could you please tell us how far away is the Croatian border from your municipality as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: I don't know, maybe 100 kilometres if you take the road, and it's a bigger distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that sabotage and terrorist units of the Croatian armies, ZNGs and others, passed through your area at that time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: I've never heard that before. You're the first one to tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And let's complete this subject. When you said Serb forces, you did not mean Serb armed formations of the Bosnian Serbs from the Republika Srpska, you meant the JNA mostly composed of the Serbian troops?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: As I said at that time they all wore JNA uniforms which for me meant that they belonged to the Republika Srpska. That's how I interpreted it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, we have to be precise. When you say Serb forces, please do not hold this against me. This is my legal problem. When one refers to Serb forces, then my police that chases up those Serb forces is not called the Serb forces and that's renegades are called Serb forces. You're talking about people of Serbian ethnicity, members of the JNA, in March?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075
utterances.text: Yes, in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, did you want to say something about the time? Do you have a decision on the time? We can go on working longer, if you give me more time, I'm prepared to work longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for today. Sir, I thought we could conclude your evidence today but things turned out not to be the case. So we have to continue on Monday, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would appreciate if we could finish today but if not, Mr. Karadzic, we will finish on Monday. There are other Mondays before us, so, yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, probably you have been told but you're not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
